newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHENS BOURSE SEEN RESUMING TRADE MONDAY.
newsitem.headline: ATHENS BOURSE SEEN RESUMING TRADE MONDAY.

text.p: Athens stock exchange member Delta Securities was in the red with the bourse's clearing house for 2.6 billion drachmas, more than the 1.2 billion initially reported, said a high-level official at the national economy ministry.
Delta was again unable to meet its settlement obligations on Friday as the Athens bourse halted trade after a boycott vote by member brokerages.

But any shareholder losses arising from Delta Securities settlement problem would be covered by the exchange's guarantee fund, said the general secretary of the national economy ministry Antonis Fotiadis after a meeting with Athens stock exchange member brokers.
But he made clear that the state would not pick up the tab nor guarantee any future losses arising from settlement incidents.
The national economy ministry would consider legislative measures aimed to improve the operating mechanisms of the stock exchange and discourage regulatory violations.
He said the meeting produced consensus on the need to bolster the bourse and strengthen its role in the country's economic growth.
Fotiadis said the Athens bourse would operate normally on Monday and that the settlement problem would be cleared up over the weekend. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
